topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology course, outlines the interdisciplinary audience, and presents the lecture's core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Biological basis of cancer as a failure of differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core concept of cancer as a progressive failure of cellular differentiation and tissue organization arising from accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes, alongside the experimental models used to study it.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and benign-to-malignant tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how tumors are distinguished as benign or malignant through the biological and histological processes of local tissue invasion, metastatic dissemination, and stepwise progression.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature conventions and exceptions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard pathological rules and notable exceptions used to name benign and malignant tumors based on their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the physiological, mechanical, and systemic mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors cause illness and death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence across humans and other animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of tumor occurrence across human populations, companion animals, and diverse taxa to illustrate cancer as a universal consequence of multicellularity.

topics.label: Principles and clinical modalities of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical rationale, diagnostic methods, benefits, and limitations of population screening and early detection across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a review of learning outcomes and practical session reminders.
